title: Cultural variation in correspondence bias: The critical role of attitude diagnosticity of socially constrained behavior
central_claims: Both cultures show correspondence bias when constrained behavior remains diagnostic.
Under minimally diagnostic behavior Americans retain correspondence bias but Japanese do not; online inferences partly mediate.

sources.title: Cultural variation in correspondence bias: The critical role of attitude diagnosticity of socially constrained behavior
sources.finding: Original text identifies broader thesis beyond the selected replication comparison.

sources.title: Many Labs 2: Investigating Variation in Replicability Across Samples and Settings
sources.finding: Strong aggregate correspondence bias and persuasiveness moderation; aggregate main effect does not itself test the original American–Japanese difference.

sources.title: Cultural Differences in Correspondence Bias Are Systematic and Multifaceted
sources.finding: Original authors analyze independent ML2 data with held-out confirmation: US bias exceeds Japanese bias, p=.008, d=.63; persuasiveness and consensus moderate cultural differences.

answers.rationale: ML2 main analysis supports generic correspondence bias, whereas the original cultural difference is explicitly tested in the original authors’ held-out reanalysis. The evidence inspected does not establish a fully independent analysis of the complete cultural/diagnosticity thesis.

search_log.purpose: Verify original thesis and read primary author text
Find claim-specific independent outcomes and contrary evidence
Inspect original-author response and exact cultural contrast

search_gaps: Blind repeat: first researcher grades and drafts were not inspected.
A positive selected replication does not validate every central claim.
Downstream operational adoption and practical utility were not established.
summary: The original US–Japan difference is recovered in original-author held-out analysis of independent ML2 data. The generic pooled bias result alone would not validate that cultural thesis. Independent-author confirmation and downstream application remain uncertain.
